tables.name: segmentation_rules
tables.purpose: Stores each merchant-defined segmentation rule with its conditions, target tag, and a version counter incremented on every edit.

columns.name: conditions
columns.purpose: Structured representation of all conditions (spend threshold, order count threshold, country filter)

columns.name: target_tag
columns.purpose: The Shopify customer tag this rule applies when a customer matches

columns.name: version
columns.purpose: Monotonically incremented each time the rule is edited

tables.name: rule_runs
tables.purpose: Tracks every execution of a segmentation rule, recording its lifecycle state, the rule version applied, and the outcome summary.

columns.name: rule_id
columns.constraints: NOT NULL REFERENCES segmentation_rules(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
columns.purpose: The segmentation rule this run belongs to

columns.name: rule_version_snapshot
columns.purpose: The rule version number at the moment the run was triggered

columns.name: newly_tagged_count
columns.purpose: Number of customers newly tagged during this run; null until the run completes

columns.name: failure_reason
columns.purpose: Human-readable reason the run failed; null for successful runs

platformGaps.gap: Shopify's tagsAdd mutation operates on a single resource per call; there is no batch mutation to tag multiple customers in one API round-trip.
platformGaps.mitigation: The recipe iterates over matching customers in a for_each loop, calling tagsAdd once per customer; per-item failures are caught and logged individually without aborting the entire batch.
platformGaps.uxImplication: For large matching sets (thousands of customers) the run will take proportionally longer; the admin UI should show a running spinner and poll /runs/status until a terminal state is returned.

platformGaps.gap: The handler processes the entire run synchronously within a single HTTP request; very large customer catalogs combined with many matching customers may approach request timeout limits.
platformGaps.mitigation: graphqlPaginate fetches customers in pages of 250 per Shopify call, and per-item tagsAdd mutations are issued sequentially within the same request; merchants with extremely large catalogs are advised to scope conditions narrowly to reduce match counts.
platformGaps.uxImplication: The admin UI must display a loading state while /runs/start is in flight and use /runs/status polling as a fallback in case the connection drops before the response is received.

uxExpectations.admin: The admin panel should present a rule list as the primary view with a clear 'Run Now' button per rule; after clicking Run Now the UI should display an inline spinner tied to the run_id and automatically show the newly_tagged_count badge once the run completes — failed runs should show the failure_reason prominently so the merchant can diagnose and retry.

edgeCases: A rule is deleted while a run for it is still in flight — the run record is cascade-deleted from rule_runs; the in-flight handler will attempt to write the completed outcome to a now-missing run_id, which silently produces zero affected rows; the Shopify tags already applied remain and are not rolled back.

Two concurrent requests to /runs/start for the same rule arrive simultaneously — both create separate run records each capturing the same rule version_snapshot; both proceed independently through their own sql_claim transition and produce separate result rows; deduplication is handled per-run by reading live tags from Shopify at fetch time.

The segmentation_rules.conditions JSONB contains unrecognized keys beyond min_spend_cents, min_order_count, and country_code — the evaluate step ignores unknown keys; the rule effectively has no conditions on those dimensions and matches customers freely on the remaining criteria.

A Shopify customer's amountSpent.amount is a string with more than two decimal places — Math.round(parseFloat(amount) * 100) always produces an integer cent value; no floating-point drift affects the threshold comparison.

A run is stuck in running state due to a process crash — the rule_runs index on status allows an operator or recovery script to SELECT * FROM rule_runs WHERE status = 'running' AND started_at < now() - INTERVAL '10 minutes' and issue a manual UPDATE to failed with an appropriate failure_reason.

The merchant updates a rule's conditions between triggering one run and triggering a second — each run row captures rule_version_snapshot at creation time so the audit trail always reflects which exact conditions produced which outcome; the two runs are fully independent.
